title: Shader Gallery Exhibition Hall
prompt:
Use Three.js to build a "gallery" room (floor + walls + ceiling), with 6 PlaneGeometry "picture frames" mounted on the walls. Each frame must use a different ShaderMaterial (an animated pattern in the fragment shader based on uv + time, with no duplicates). Support clicking a painting to view it enlarged (via a camera tween or picture-in-picture), global animation speed adjustment, and an FPS display.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Interaction]
(1) The 6 paintings have indices 0..5 and are selected by clicking with a Raycaster; selectedPainting must be number|null, where null indicates no selection/gallery mode.
(2) Enlarged-view interaction: the implementation may determine whether clicking empty space again or pressing ESC closes it, but the state must remain synchronized.
(3) id="speedSlider": a range input mapped to each shader's uniform time multiplier or to a global timeScale.
(4) FPS: write a moving average of frame intervals to __3D_STATE__.fps.

[State Exposure (Required)]
window.__3D_STATE__ = {
  paintingCount: number,     // Always 6
  selectedPainting: number | null,
  speed: number,             // Consistent with speedSlider
  fps: number
}

[Evaluation Helper (Required, for StateProbe)]
(5) window.__STATEPROBE_selectPainting__(i: number | null): equivalent to clicking painting i (0..5); pass null to exit the enlarged view/cancel the selection.

Output a single HTML file that can run when opened directly in a browser.
